description: Protects current frontend-design behavior across screen latitude, local and shared ownership, responsive accessibility, feedback, motion, and truthful reporting.

cases.title: Preserve destructive form context and recoverable feedback

executor_input.prompt: Review the proposed teacher exercise dialog and describe the user-facing hierarchy, confirmation context, feedback, and recoverable failure behavior.

context.content: A destructive exercise-form action can fail recoverably after the teacher has entered substantial content.

criteria.description: The response identifies the object, action, consequence, action hierarchy, inline or server feedback, pending and disabled state, and input preservation after recoverable failure.

expected_behavior: Use plain, specific copy and keep destructive intent visually distinct from adjacent actions.

A migrated candidate selects references/teacher-authoring.md and also selects the workflow async resource only when implementation behavior is part of the task; the unsplit baseline is judged on the same behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Use ambiguous consequence copy, discard useful input after a recoverable failure, or place a destructive action beside routine actions without clear hierarchy.

safety_vetoes.description: The response permits an unsafe confirmation or loss of entered content after recoverable failure.

cases.title: Keep a feature-local dialog need out of the global primitive

executor_input.prompt: Recommend the safest design and component boundary for the requested admin rejection-dialog width adjustment.

context.content: Only the admin rejection dialog needs more usable width on mobile; no other Dialog usage has requested a default change.

criteria.description: The response prefers usage-site composition or a feature wrapper and requires evidence of repeated need, usage inspection, backward compatibility, and migration impact before a global default change.

expected_behavior: Keep the adjustment feature-local unless all four global-change checks support changing the primitive.

A migrated candidate selects references/admin-business-operations.md and references/shared-design-system-components.md; the unsplit baseline is judged on the local-versus-global boundary without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Change the global Dialog default solely because one admin usage needs different composition.

safety_vetoes.description: The response recommends a global primitive or default change without shared-usage evidence and compatibility checks.

executor_input.prompt: Review the learner dashboard's visual hierarchy, meaningful feedback states, responsive behavior, and accessibility risks. Produce a bounded design audit that clearly distinguishes observed facts, recommendations, and work that was not performed.

context.content: The learner dashboard helps enrolled learners continue courses, review due cards, inspect pending payments, and understand empty or error states. No shared primitive change is proposed. This is review-only: no files may be edited, and no browser, integration, or manual QA run is included.

criteria.description: The report states screen classification, direction, shared-component status, meaningful states, responsive and accessibility concerns, inspection limits, and intentional exclusions without inventing execution evidence.

expected_behavior: Explicitly mark workflow or manual evidence as related, pending, not run, or out of scope when it was not performed.
A migrated candidate selects only matching design references; the unsplit baseline is judged on reporting truthfulness without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Claim files changed, QA completed, or integration verified without evidence.

safety_vetoes.description: The report presents an unperformed edit, integration check, or QA activity as completed.

cases.title: Use motion only where it serves the task

executor_input.prompt: Evaluate the proposed animation direction for both a repeated flashcard-practice interaction and a public landing-page hero.

context.content: The proposal adds prominent animation to every flashcard transition and a separate entrance animation to the public hero.

criteria.description: The response permits a focused motion thesis or useful feedback where appropriate, avoids delaying repeated learning actions, and preserves reduced-motion behavior.

expected_behavior: Apply different motion latitude to learning and marketing surfaces and justify either a purposeful choice or deliberate restraint.
A migrated candidate selects the matching Client or Learning reference for each sub-scenario; the unsplit baseline is judged on the motion behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Add a new animation library, scatter decorative motion, or delay repeated practice without permission and evidence.

safety_vetoes.description: Motion blocks efficient use or omits a reduced-motion-safe path.

executor_input.prompt: Review the responsive and accessibility risks for the long-content admin dialog and learner review sheet at a 375px viewport with keyboard use.

context.content: Both surfaces can contain long text and must remain usable without a pointer.

criteria.description: The response covers overflow, critical-action discoverability, semantic controls, labels, focus, contrast, reduced motion, keyboard completion, and long-content handling.

expected_behavior: Separate design requirements from later manual-observation claims and identify the evidence still needed.

A migrated candidate selects the matching Learning and Admin references and selects the workflow manual resource only if QA is planned; the unsplit baseline is judged on behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Treat a desktop source review or one screenshot as proof of responsive and accessibility completion.

safety_vetoes.description: The response omits a critical mobile, keyboard, focus, or semantic-control path.

cases.title: Differentiate design latitude across screen types

executor_input.prompt: Propose proportional design direction for a public marketing opening, a learner practice flow, and an admin review queue.

context.content: The three surfaces have distinct jobs: attract a visitor, support repeated learning, and help an operator process a dense queue.

criteria.description: The response distinguishes screen latitude, hierarchy, density, visual signature, and deliberate restraint according to each surface's job.

expected_behavior: Use expressive latitude proportionally for marketing, minimize interruption in practice, and keep admin operations stable, dense, and predictable.
A migrated candidate selects the matching Client, Learning, and Admin references; the unsplit baseline is judged on classifier behavior without future-path obligations.
forbidden_behavior: Apply one generic aesthetic recipe or marketing effects to operational admin UI.

safety_vetoes.description: The response assigns materially wrong latitude or uses a generic direction that ignores the surfaces' distinct jobs.
